scope-authored.description: GOAL.md and DEMO.md exist at docs/plan/adhd-build/ and together cover: the 10 problem statements, the target demo sequence, the definition of done, and all non-goals
scope-authored.rationale: Every research dispatch reads these files as its primary context. Without them an agent receives only its milestone description and will research in the wrong direction or produce generic output.

research-cli-ux.description: Decision record: chosen interactive CLI library, with rationale covering Q&A loop, loading states, progress lines, and amend prompts; includes a minimal working code sample
research-cli-ux.rationale: The cli-shell milestone cannot be scoped until we know whether the interactive surface is mostly library configuration or bespoke construction. Wrong choice here = rewrite.

research-llm-structured-output.description: Decision record: most reliable mechanism for getting structured question+answer arrays back from an LLM call — tool use vs JSON mode vs constrained decoding — with failure mode analysis and chosen approach
research-llm-structured-output.rationale: The ground-plan agent returns a structured list of questions with suggested answers. The reliability of parsing determines the entire llm-adapter contract. A wrong assumption here causes silent malformed output at runtime.

research-dag-orchestration.description: Decision record: build the dispatcher from scratch vs adopt an existing DAG orchestration tool; if adopting, specifies which tool, what it handles, and what gap remains
research-dag-orchestration.rationale: Building a correct topological sort + parallel wave executor + state writer is non-trivial. If Temporal, BullMQ, or a lighter tool already covers it, the dispatcher milestone scope changes dramatically.

research-parallel-llm-dispatch.description: Decision record: pattern for parallel LLM call dispatch in Node.js — worker threads vs async Promise.all vs a task queue — covering back-pressure, failure isolation, and token budget enforcement
research-parallel-llm-dispatch.rationale: The execution-loop dispatches multiple milestones in parallel. Without knowing the right concurrency model, the dispatcher core will either serialize everything (slow) or have races and dropped results (broken).

dag-schema.description: dag.json TypeScript types, read/write helpers, and a validator that enforces: all pending milestones have resolver upstreams, no dependency cycles, all operations on pending:null milestones have shape, terminal milestone is reachable
dag-schema.rationale: Every other component reads or writes dag.json. A shared typed schema with a validator is the foundation — without it, each component invents its own parsing and silent corruption is undetectable.

dispatcher-core.description: Non-LLM orchestration engine: reads dag.json, computes eligible milestones (pending: null + deps complete), assigns wave numbers, writes dispatch_log entries, updates operation statuses, surfaces non-blocking questions
dispatcher-core.rationale: The dispatcher is the only component that drives plan execution. It must never call an LLM itself — it only reads dag.json state and decides what to fire next. This is the system's reliability backbone.
dispatcher-core.pending: dag-orchestration research decision: build vs adopt, and if adopt, which tool and what interface does it expose

llm-adapter.description: Adapter that takes a packaged dispatch unit (operations[], context, model, effort) and returns structured results per operation; handles tool use or JSON mode depending on research decision; retries on malformed output
llm-adapter.rationale: This is the only component that talks to a model provider. Isolating it means every other component is testable without LLM calls, and the provider can be swapped without touching orchestration logic.
llm-adapter.pending: structured-output research decision: tool use vs JSON mode, and exact schema for question/answer arrays

ground-plan-agent.description: Prompt + structured output spec for the first LLM dispatch: reads goal file, returns (a) questions with suggested answers and (b) on second pass with Q&A filled in, returns milestone stubs with descriptions, rationale, depends_on, guard, and pending where unknown
ground-plan-agent.rationale: This is the only planning-specific agent in the system. It converts an unstructured goal into a structured dag.json skeleton. Its output format must be machine-parseable — no prose, only typed fields.
ground-plan-agent.pending: structured-output decision needed to define question/answer schema and milestone stub format

scaffolding.description: `adhd-build <goal-path>` parses the goal file, derives a slug, creates docs/plan/<slug>/, writes a skeleton dag.json with plan-level fields populated, and fires the first ground-plan dispatch
scaffolding.rationale: This is the entry point a user touches. It must be idempotent (re-running on an existing plan resumes, doesn't overwrite), produce a valid dag.json on first run, and give the user immediate feedback that something is happening.

cli-shell.description: Interactive shell surface: loading/progress lines, Q&A loop (answer / skip / use suggested), milestone summary display, 'Execute or amend?' prompt, non-blocking question surfacing during execution, completion summaries
cli-shell.rationale: The CLI is the only human-facing component. It translates every dispatcher event into a shell line. It must never drive logic — it only renders state from dag.json and passes user input back to the dispatcher.
cli-shell.pending: cli-ux research decision: which library, and whether Q&A loop and progress display are configuration or construction

amend-interface.description: Amendment flow: at 'Execute or amend?' the user can specify a playbook to apply before a named milestone; the system patches dag.json to insert the playbook's milestones as upstreams of the target and re-renders the milestone summary
amend-interface.rationale: This is the human escape hatch. Without it, the user has no way to reshape the plan after ground-plan generates it. It must operate by mutating dag.json — not by re-running ground-plan — so the existing milestone work is preserved.
amend-interface.pending: are playbooks named built-in patterns the system ships with, or files the user authors? — asked of user during planning session, not yet answered

system-end-to-end.description: Full run from goal file to completed plan: adhd-build → ground-plan → Q&A → milestones → amend → execute → completion summary. Two fixtures: a clean run and a run with a guard failure + correction loop.
system-end-to-end.rationale: Unit tests on each component don't prove the system works end-to-end. This milestone runs the full demo flow and verifies the dag.json state at each transition matches expected shape.
system-end-to-end.guard: npx tsx scripts/test-e2e.ts --fixture fixtures/e2e-clean.json && npx tsx scripts/test-e2e.ts --fixture fixtures/e2e-correction.json

open_questions.text: Are playbooks named built-in patterns the system ships with, or files the user authors?
